body.heading: Where in the world is Benin?
paragraphs: Benin is a country in Western Africa, which is part of Africa.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Benin is Porto-Novo. Porto-Novo is the capital, and the government works in Cotonou, the biggest city and main port, a short drive away.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: People in Benin speak French and Fon. Fon is the home language of many families in the south; French is the official language of school and government.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Benin is the West African CFA franc. The CFA franc is shared with neighbouring countries, so the same money works across the region.

body.heading: How big is Benin?
paragraphs: Benin covers about 113,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. That makes it about twice the size of Togo.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: In Ganvie, whole streets are water! Families ride in wooden canoes between houses built on stilts above Lake Nokoué, where people shop, fish and go to school by boat.
Ouidah is a historic town of temples and old forts. Its famous memorial arch, the Door of No Return, helps families remember an important and difficult part of history.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Find Benin on a map or globe. Which continent is it on — and can you name a country that sits next to it?
2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?
